heroSubhead: Live mountain conditions from Bowman Mtn, the Twins, and West Ridge. Webcams, air quality, and ground temps — updated every 5 minutes.

general.label: General Information
paragraphs: This project is a live mountain conditions feed for Bowman Ridge, N Twin, and the west ridge corridor along the Middle Fork Area. It exists to make route planning safer and more informed.
AQI is currently reported at two locations (Bowman Mtn and N Twin), with additional temperature context from ridge sensors and the Dailey Prairie ground station.

I keep a Middle Fork field guide of area notes and references, compiled from available sources, not an official historical record. A companion write-up on Twins weather and sensors covers how the ridge instruments relate to what you see on the cameras.

nerdy.label: Nerdy Stuff
paragraphs: Basics: three types of equipment — gateways, sensors, and cameras. A cellular gateway relays LoRaWAN sensor packets to The Things Network. The cameras are trail cams (GardePro, Vosker, and a Tachyon on Bowman Ridge) that upload over cellular; this page is their gallery.

Sensors include off-the-shelf LoRaWAN units (battery and solar) and custom weather/AQI nodes built on Particle Boron MCUs. Newer Muon-based units add cellular alongside LoRaWAN for better reliability when coverage is thin. AQI on the ridge stations is mainly for summer smoke season.
There is also a seismic node — Mount Baker is an active volcano, so why not? More on how the instruments relate to the cameras: Twins weather and sensors.
